name: Timer dial
intent: Bound the session and each phase in time, so deliberation ends in a decision.
when: work that expands to fill the time available, or a decision that keeps being deferred
prompt: Divide the sitting into phases on the dial; move the marker as each phase ends.
readback: Where the marker stopped tells you which phase was over-run — usually the one that was hardest to face.

claims.claim: Setting a fixed time limit for a phase of work ends deliberation sooner, with no loss of decision quality for convergent tasks.
Time pressure during idea generation reduces creative, divergent output.
claims.construct: time pressure and creativity (challenge vs hindrance stressors)

grounding.helps: when a convergent decision is being turned over long after new information has stopped arriving: a written stop time is a craft practice for forcing a choice, not a tested method
grounding.backfires: when the stop is set on idea generation, where time pressure is the known risk, or on a decision that needs every option weighed; nothing read shows a timebox leaves decision quality intact
